name: Veli Tourist Village (Veli Lagoon)
tagline: Lagoon gardens, floating bridge and calm evening promenades by the sea
summary: Veli Tourist Village sits where Veli Lake meets the Arabian Sea, offering gardens, pedal-boating, a floating café and an easy evening promenade—pleasant in Kerala's winter months.
description: Veli Tourist Village occupies the estuarine edge where Veli Lake (Veli Kayal) opens into the Arabian Sea. The site combines landscaped gardens, a floating bridge to the beach, play areas and small water-activity facilities that make it a popular picnic and family spot near Thiruvananthapuram.

The lagoon setting gives visitors both backwater calm and sea views in one place; there are pedal boats, a children's park, sculptures by Kanayi Kunhiraman and a floating café run by tourism authorities. Walkways and seating make it especially pleasant for late-afternoon and evening strolls.

The village is close to the city and airport, so it is easy as a half-day outing or an evening stop. Visitors looking for quiet lagoon views, short boat rides, or a breezy seaside walk find Veli an accessible, low-effort addition to a Kovalam–Varkala circuit.
highlights: Landscape gardens beside the Veli lagoon
Floating bridge linking the garden to Veli Beach
Pedal/paddle boating and small boat hire on the lagoon
Children’s park, floating café and public seating
Easy evening promenade with lagoon + sea views

sections.heading: Background
body: Veli Tourist Village is a development around the mouth of Veli Lake where the freshwater lagoon meets the Arabian Sea. The site is managed as a public picnic and leisure area with gardens, play zones and small water-activity facilities maintained by local tourism bodies.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Stroll the landscaped gardens and cross the floating bridge to the beach for combined lagoon-and-sea scenery. Short pedal-boat rides and supervised small-boat trips explore the calm inner waters; sculptures and children’s play equipment make it family-friendly.

Evening promenades along the waterfront are popular when winds are gentle—watch fishermen, feeding birds and the changing light on the lagoon. The floating café and nearby stalls offer simple snacks; for longer visits combine Veli with nearby Aakkulam or Shankumugham.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Kerala Tourism lists the main entrance timing as 08:00–18:30 and publishes modest entry fees (adult and child categories); confirm current hours, activity availability and ticketing before you travel. Boat rides, horse rides and the miniature train (when running) usually charge extra.

Veli is a short drive (about 10–12 km) from central Thiruvananthapuram and close to the airport; it works well as a half-day or evening outing. Facilities are basic—use local transport or private vehicle for best flexibility and confirm any seasonal service schedules in advance.

latest.text: A new solar-powered passenger‑cum‑tourism boat service on the Parvathy Puthanar, linking Veli and Kadinamkulam, is inaugurated; initial services and fare details were published at launch.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November–February (cool, drier months—pleasant evenings and walks)
visitorInfo.howToReach: About 10–12 km from Thiruvananthapuram city; reachable by local bus, auto-rickshaw or taxi. Close to the international airport and short drive from Kochuveli rail station—confirm local connections for the last mile.
etiquette: Confirm boat, miniature-train and floating-café timings before you go—services run seasonally and may change.
Evening sea breezes can be cool in winter—carry a light layer for sunset walks.
Respect local fishing areas and avoid entering open sea when tides are high; supervise children near water.
Carry small change for entry fees, rides and stall food; facilities are public and basic.
